chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad al-Abdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition except that which strengthens the bone and grows the flesh. As for the single feeding, the two feedings, and the three feedings, up to ten, if they are separate, there is no objection."
And that which I rely upon in this chapter, and upon which action should be taken, is the narration which he narrated.

key_terms.أَنْبَتَ اللَّحْمَ: Grows the flesh (a criterion for substantial feeding)
key_terms.الرِّضَاعُ: Breastfeeding (the act that establishes kinship prohibition)
key_terms.شَدَّ الْعَظْمَ: Strengthens the bone (a criterion for substantial feeding)
key_terms.مُتَفَرِّقَاتٍ: Separate/distinct (feedings not consumed in one sitting)

ai.seo_question: How many separate breastfeedings are required to establish marital prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the threshold for *radha'* (breastfeeding) establishing *mahramiyyah*, specifying that only substantial nursing that 'strengthens bone and flesh' creates prohibition, while fragmented feedings of up to ten times do not. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights this specific report as the preferred basis for legal practice (*al-'amal*), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between minor and significant nursing events to determine kinship ties.
